MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools work by providing a standardized way for AI applications to connect to various tools and data sources uniformly. An MCP server exposes tools (functions the AI model can call), resources (readable data), and prompts (reusable templates). An MCP client embedded in the AI app connects to one or more MCP servers, discovers their available tools, and makes those tools accessible to the AI agent.

When the client connects to a server, it requests a list of tools, each described by a name, a human-readable description, and a JSON schema of its arguments. The AI agent uses this information to decide which tool to call and how to provide the necessary arguments. The client forwards the tool call to the server, which executes it and returns the result to the model.

This standardized interface allows the same MCP server to be used across different agents and frameworks, enabling tools and agents to evolve independently and making it easy to add new capabilities by connecting additional servers.
